limitations: Owned assumed-role GetFunction returned AccessDeniedException on all 15 attempts despite a successful scoped inline allow policy write. Native errors say no identity-based policy allows the action; the cause was not established. No successful owned-role download URL was issued, so caller Lambda permission revocation remains unobserved; the real caller's policies were never changed.

HTTP requests sample discrete instants; object retention beyond the last successful pre-expiry download is not directly observable after authorization expiry. Only one tiny ZIP function in us-east-1 was tested; no invocation, published version, alias, image package or customer-managed KMS key was used.

metadata: GetFunction succeeded in both Pending and Active states and included Code.Location in each.

Unqualified, explicit Qualifier=$LATEST and FunctionName suffix :$LATEST succeeded. Matching suffix plus qualifier succeeded. Conflicting name or ARN suffix versus Qualifier returned service InvalidParameterValueException with the derived-qualifier mismatch message.

Unqualified GetFunction omitted Concurrency with no reservation and after release; it included ReservedConcurrentExecutions=0 and =1 while those reservations existed. Explicit Qualifier=$LATEST omitted Concurrency even while the unqualified response exposed reservation 1.
http: The same issued URL returned GET 200, HEAD 403 with no body, and GET Range bytes=0-31 returned 206 with the exact requested uploaded bytes. The URL signed headers were host only; adding this bounded Range did not invalidate authorization. HEAD failure establishes method-sensitive behavior but exposes no XML error code.

Full downloads matched the uploaded original 197-byte ZIP or updated 196-byte ZIP byte-for-byte, with SHA-256 values also matching native Configuration.CodeSha256. Content-Type was application/zip, Accept-Ranges was bytes, ETag matched the corresponding uploaded ZIP MD5, and ranged responses exposed Content-Range.
artifact_lifecycle: The original URL kept returning the original ZIP immediately after UpdateFunctionCode and after its successful completion. A fresh GetFunction URL returned the updated ZIP instead.

After confirmed function and execution-role deletion, both issued URLs continued returning their respective deployment bytes. The original URL still returned its original ZIP at signature age 590 seconds, over 530 seconds after function deletion.

The original URL advertised X-Amz-Expires=599 and returned AccessDenied / Request has expired at signature age 605 seconds and again at 660 seconds. The fresh URL advertised 600 seconds; it still returned updated bytes while the original URL was already expired, then returned the same expiry error after its own deadline.

Download URLs therefore address retained deployment artifacts independently of the current function record or current code. An implementation that resolves old downloads only through current-function lookup, replaces old bytes on update, or revokes downloads immediately on deletion would contradict these observations. Retention beyond authorization expiry is not established.
